questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wished to study a place, where they would offer different classes from what I am offered at home, but still classes that are relevant to my study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience in Istanbul. The city is very interesting, and I learned a lot. I also found some very good friends, which was great fun. I had perhaps expected more from the education, but I was very happy with what I got out of my exchange semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy with help from the Erasmus Office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My buddy and Erasmus Office helped me with everything I needed. I got help with registration and visa etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, I just rented and AirBnB. I can recommend doing that or joining FB-groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It isn't lonely to live alone off campus, as you will make many friends during your stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were dorms available, however they were very strict, and I didn't meet anyone who chose to live there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy with the help I got. If not, I would have had trouble figuring everything out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had many papers to sign both for school and to get a residence permit. We fixed most of it within the first week – introduction week – with much help from our Erasmus buddies.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Office and our individual buddies were of big help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was luckily very successful in the end, but it took some time to get everything to fit.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the help that is offered. You will need it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't as challenging, as I would have hoped, but I took some new classes, which were very interesting, and I did learn a lot in the end.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We didn't have academic papers in the way, I am used to. Nor did we have to spend much time preparing for each class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar with classroom-teaching and groupwork.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Persuasion, Digital Media Ethics, Photography, Brand Management and Understanding Social Behaviour.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Digital Media Ethics, Photography and Brand Management.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: We had to pay for a Turkish insurance in the very beginning that we weren't aware of. This was additional to our normal insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the grocery stores were more expensive than expected. At least in normal grocery stores.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't do many social activities that weren't a part of Erasmus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not quite sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join in on the Erasmus events. It is a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the city – the mosques, the museums. Talk to people on the street and go to local places. You will learn a lot and meet a very open people.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy more often than not. I felt safe, and I got very into the culture and cultural practices. It was extremely interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to start a conversation. Turkish students are interested, and they will most likely also try to start a conversation with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Harrassment on the street.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people and the food. They were very friendly, and the food is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Travel, take classes that you find interesting, learn some Turkish

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many lovely people and experiencing an interesting culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a new culture and new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
